questions: Does steering_oscillation fall below 0.10 on the s-bend and slalom with y=0.06 m?
Is line_loss_events back to 0 on all three tracks? If not, on which track and at what max_error?
Does the s-bend keep progress near 0.15 or better, and does the slalom max_error stay below the 0.06 m limit?
Does the oval (progress 0.115, max_error 0.061 m in every iteration since 1) still end at the same point? If so, is there a fixed feature of that track that geometry alone cannot fix?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If steering_oscillation is still above 0.10 at y=0.06 m, return to y=0.05 m. If the s-bend progress falls back to 0.04 m-level values, keep y=0.06 m and tell me so the lead can be found between 0.06 and 0.07 m. Report the per-track progress and max_error for the oval, since its failure has not moved across three iterations.

intent: Find the forward sensor lead that keeps the s-bend gain from iteration 3 while removing its line loss and steering jitter. Move the sensor row from y=0.07 m back to y=0.06 m, holding every other geometry field fixed, so the race isolates the lead change against iteration 3's 51.31.
learning: Iteration 3 raised the score through the s-bend and slalom but not the oval, and it brought back line loss and jitter above 0.10 steering oscillation. The lead is a real lever for bend progress, but y=0.07 m looks too aggressive. Next I test the midpoint y=0.06 m with everything else unchanged.
rationale: Iteration 3 scored 51.31, up from 26.64. The gain came almost entirely from the s-bend and slalom: s-bend progress rose from 0.040 to 0.155 and rms_error fell to 0.024 m. The oval is unchanged at progress 0.115 and max_error 0.061 m across iterations 1 to 3, so the oval failure point does not respond to sensor lead, mass or track width. Iteration 3 also brought back line loss (1 event each on s-bend and slalom) and pushed steering_oscillation to 0.127 (s-bend) and 0.138 (slalom), above the 0.10 threshold the Integrator set. Slalom max_error of 0.065 m is past the 0.06 m off-track limit. I read the y=0.07 lead as the cause of the jitter and line loss: it helped the bends but overshoots. Per the Integrator's rule (oscillation above 0.1 with max_error still at or above 0.06 m), I pull the sensor row back, but not all the way to y=0.05. The lead was useful on the s-bend, so I pick the midpoint y=0.06 and keep everything else from iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09, mass 0.5, body 0.12 x 0.12, +/-0.05 m spread, 16 mm footprints). Changing one variable keeps the result attributable to the lead alone. Expected result: steering_oscillation falls to about 0.09 to 0.11, line_loss_events drops toward 0, and the s-bend keeps most of its progress gain (above 0.12). Oval max_error should stay near 0.06 m. I hold wheel_radius at 0.03 m for now, since the Integrator's speed change (0.04 m) would confound the lead test; I will raise it next if progress stays below 0.2 and max_error stays at or above 0.06 m.
